sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Write the names of the scientists: (a) Who discovered the C3 cycle. (b) Who showed that isolated chloroplasts release oxygen in light.
questions.answer: (a) Melvin Calvin. (b) Robert Hill (the Hill reaction).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The initial CO2 acceptor in the C3 cycle is ______. (b) The initial CO2 acceptor in the C4 cycle is ______.
questions.answer: (a) RuBP (ribulose bisphosphate). (b) PEP (phosphoenolpyruvate).

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Oxygen is evolved in cyclic photophosphorylation. (b) NADPH2 and ATP are the assimilatory power.
questions.answer: (a) False. (b) True.

questions.q: Match: (a) P680 (b) P700 with (i) PS I (ii) PS II.
Name the two phases of photosynthesis and where each occurs.
questions.answer: Light reaction in the thylakoids (grana) and dark reaction in the stroma.

questions.q: Name the pigment groups: (a) chlorophyll a and b (b) carotene and xanthophyll.
questions.answer: (a) Chlorophylls. (b) Carotenoids.

questions.q: Give two examples of C4 plants.
questions.answer: Sugarcane and maize.

questions.q: In which regions of the spectrum is photosynthesis maximum and minimum?
questions.answer: Maximum in blue and red light; minimum in green and yellow light.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is photophosphorylation?
questions.answer: The formation of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate using the energy released during electron flow in the light reaction.

questions.q: Differentiate between the absorption spectrum and the action spectrum.
questions.answer: The absorption spectrum shows the absorbance of different wavelengths by a pigment; the action spectrum shows the effectiveness of different wavelengths in driving photosynthesis.

questions.q: What is Kranz anatomy? In which plants is it found?
questions.answer: A wreath-like arrangement of large bundle sheath cells around the vascular bundles with dimorphic chloroplasts, found in C4 plants such as maize and sugarcane.

questions.q: State Blackman's law of limiting factors.
questions.answer: When a process depends on several factors, its rate is limited by the factor which is at the lowest level (the slowest factor).

questions.q: Write the overall equation of photosynthesis.
questions.answer: 6CO2 + 12H2O gives C6H12O6 + 6H2O + 6O2 in the presence of light and chlorophyll.

questions.q: What is photolysis? Where does it occur?
questions.answer: The light-dependent splitting of water into H+, electrons and O2, which occurs in PS II inside the thylakoid.

questions.q: Mention two internal factors affecting photosynthesis.
questions.answer: Amount of chlorophyll and leaf age and anatomy.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between PS I and PS II (three points).
questions.answer: PS I has reaction centre P700 and an Fe-S protein as primary acceptor and reduces NADP; PS II has reaction centre P680 and pheophytin as primary acceptor and splits water to release O2.

questions.q: Explain the role of light in the formation of assimilatory power.
questions.answer: Light excites the electrons of PS II and PS I; as they pass down the electron transport chain ATP is formed and at the end NADP is reduced to NADPH2; these two (ATP and NADPH2) are the assimilatory power used to fix CO2.

questions.q: Write any three differences between the light and dark reactions.
questions.answer: The light reaction needs light, occurs in the thylakoids and forms ATP and NADPH2 with release of O2; the dark reaction occurs in the stroma, uses ATP and NADPH2 to fix CO2 into sugar and is not directly light dependent.

questions.q: Explain the importance of photosynthesis.
questions.answer: It converts light energy into chemical energy, provides food to all organisms, releases oxygen and fossil fuels are its ancient products.

questions.q: Explain the structure of C4 leaf and its significance.
questions.answer: Bundle sheath cells wreath the vascular bundles; mesophyll chloroplasts are granal without starch and bundle sheath chloroplasts are agranal with starch; the arrangement concentrates CO2 and prevents photorespiration, so the plant can grow in hot, dry conditions.

questions.q: Describe the C4 pathway briefly.
questions.answer: In the mesophyll, PEP combines with CO2 (PEP carboxylase) to form OAA; it is converted into a C4 acid and transported to the bundle sheath, where it releases CO2 which enters the Calvin cycle to give sugars.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is photophosphorylation? Write the differences between cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
questions.answer: Photophosphorylation is the synthesis of ATP using light energy. Cyclic: only PS I; electrons return to P700; only ATP; no photolysis and no O2; in bacteria. Non-cyclic: PS II and PS I; electrons from water finally reach NADP; ATP and NADPH2 formed; photolysis and O2 evolved; in green plants.

questions.q: Name the scientists who discovered the C3 cycle in plants. Write any four differences between C3 plants and C4 plants.
questions.answer: Melvin Calvin. C3: one CO2 fixation with RuBP and Rubisco, first product PGA, no Kranz anatomy, photorespiration present, less efficient. C4: two fixations with PEP carboxylase and Rubisco, first product OAA, Kranz anatomy, no photorespiration, more efficient.

questions.q: In photosynthesis, there are two reactions: light and dark reactions. Why are they called so? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: The light reaction needs light directly: it occurs in the thylakoids, splits water and makes ATP and NADPH2. The dark reaction does not use light directly: it occurs in the stroma and fixes CO2 using the ATP and NADPH2 formed in the light reaction (it can go on in light too).

questions.q: With the help of a diagrammatic representation explain the Calvin cycle. Where does it take place?
questions.answer: In the stroma of the chloroplast: CO2 + RuBP gives 2 PGA (carboxylation by Rubisco); PGA is reduced to triose phosphate using ATP and NADPH2; some triose phosphate forms glucose, sucrose and starch; the rest regenerates RuBP using ATP.

questions.q: Explain the factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis.
questions.answer: Internal: chlorophyll, leaf age and structure, demand for photosynthate; external: light, CO2, temperature, water and minerals; Blackman's law of limiting factors says the slowest factor limits the rate.
